sprint: Phase 2 Liquid Shaper Upgrade and Dark Strobe

Abandoned OffscreenCanvas pilot, staging, unified-worker, duplicated-runtime, worker-protocol, and worker-bundling paths remain removed. Any future OffscreenCanvas work must move the production renderer rather than recreate it and requires a new explicit parity review.

Reviewed session changes remove unused audio-worker traffic, gate stereo reads, separate GPU particle controls, add renderer-internal timing quality, and do not transfer visible-renderer ownership.

phase463Review: Auto Zoom now advances from the existing scheduler-owned clamped delta and applies bounded BPM phase correction, attack/release energy smoothing, and rate-limited layer scales without a new RAF, timer, canvas, or worker. Astral and beat-shockwave timestamps use the same authoritative frame time. Orbital Energy uses a two-stroke conic-gradient path with a bounded 24-segment compatibility fallback; Halo Comet retains its approved underglow/easing with 24 overlapping tail segments; Shockwave gradients use a context-local 48-entry LRU. App.tsx, the approved Core Particle shader, and the 449-line Canvas2D Core Particle fallback remain byte-identical; visible-renderer ownership remains on the certified main thread.
phase464AReview: The legacy WebGL spike path is extracted into a dedicated WebGL2 runtime with initialization-cached state, one persistent VAO, FFT/sample-rate keyed frequency maps, one authoritative amplitude profile/upload, and two mirrored draws. Gamma is geometry-neutral and shader-owned; Iridize shell/fringe/tip color is shader-owned, so the Canvas premium overlay stays inactive during WebGL rendering. Rotation, Auto Zoom, Halo Comet and Orbital Energy consume one scheduler-clamped motion phase. Auto Zoom eases to neutral without per-frame input or pulse closures, and Orbital Energy uses a bounded normalized Path2D cache instead of per-frame conic gradients. No RAF, timer, worker, canvas, dependency, or recording behavior was added. App.tsx, the Phase 4.5 Core Particle shader, and the 449-line Canvas2D Core Particle fallback remain byte-identical.
phase48AReview: Phase 4.8A introduces a host-neutral VisualizerRenderKernel and MainThreadRenderHost without changing the production executeVisualFramePipeline body. The exact frame body SHA-256 remains 1217913c6f34efced99df0c314a13cfea5e9cb4f7407f3201feb97e0d95a7bad. RuntimeFrameEngine/foundation ownership now sits behind MainThreadRenderHost; the former createRuntimeFrameAuthority is a compatibility adapter over the same host/kernel and no longer contains a second scheduler implementation. refactorPhase3Review: Refactor Phase 3 moves the parity-frozen production frame body, its frame-local mutable state, diagnostics, certification, and existing ProductionFrameRuntime composition into one typed production-frame controller. The session entry point is reduced to setup/orchestration and explicit angle, shape-select, and Dot owner bridges. The exact production frame body hash is unchanged. sprintIntegrityLockReview: Sprint 'Integrity Lock' (2026-09-23) intentionally modifies one frozen file, src/app/runtime/visualizer/renderers/CanvasSpikeRingRenderer.ts, to (1) batch the Canvas2D spike-ring stroke submission by resolved color into one Path2D per bucket instead of one beginPath()/stroke() pair per spike, cutting per-frame paint calls from O(N) to O(bucket count) with identical geometry and color output, and (2) replace the fallback Iridize band-recolor with a fresh, additive 'Chroma Flare' pass drawn in its own hue lane past the spike tip and composited with globalCompositeOperation='lighter', so it only ever adds light/alpha on top of the existing spike rather than recoloring or dimming it; the flare is fully gated behind the existing iridize>0.01 threshold and adds zero cost when Iridize is off. The exact production frame body hash (executeVisualFramePipeline) is unchanged, as is App.tsx and the certified Core Particle fallback. No RAF, timer, worker, canvas, or per-frame object allocation was added; Path2D instances are created only per distinct color bucket touched that frame, not per spike. Separately (outside this frozen set), src/app/runtime/visualizer/setup/createRendererViewportSetup.ts had its shouldInitLegacyGL gate changed from `!CORE_PARTICLES_SANDBOX && !useWebGLCoreParticlesRef.current` to `!useWebGLCoreParticlesRef.current`, restoring legacy WebGL spike context creation (and with it GPU Spike Bloom and shader-owned Iridize per phase464AReview) whenever Core Particles isn't actively using the WebGL canvas this session; the frame controller's existing per-frame mutual-exclusivity check (useEngineOwnedGL / legacyWebGLSpikeAllowed) is unchanged and continues to arbitrate between the two GPU consumers at render time.
sprintBReview: Sprint B (2026-09-23, hot-loop performance / Worker BPM / code-splitting) touches one file inside this frozen set: src/app/runtime/visualizer/controls/registerVisualizerControlPlane.ts. The FFT-slider resize handler previously sized spikeFeature.ampBuf/ampEcho1/ampEcho2/tempSmoothingBuf to `audioBuffers.timeArr.length` (analyser.fftSize, the time-domain length) while the frame loop's spike count N is `filteredFreqArr.length` (analyser.frequencyBinCount, exactly half); the two never matched, so the careful linear-interpolation resample this handler performs was discarded one frame later when the frame controller's own `ampBuf.length !== N` mismatch check fired and re-resized with a cruder nearest-neighbor copy. `newLength` now reads `analyser.frequencyBinCount` directly, matching N, so the sizes agree and the redundant second allocation/resample no longer happens on every FFT slider change. No spike geometry, amplitude sampling, or frequency mapping formula was touched. (An IntroTutorial React.lazy()/Suspense code-split in App.tsx was attempted and then reverted in the same sprint, after verify-dist-output.mjs's 'Figma-safe eager UI boundary' check correctly flagged it — that check has no override path in this codebase and its history wasn't visible to us, so App.tsx was restored to its exact pre-sprint static-import form rather than bypassing it; App.tsx is unchanged from the prior sprint.) Neither remaining change touches the exact production frame body (executeVisualFramePipeline, hash unchanged), RAF ownership, or the certified Core Particle fallback.
sprintCHotfixReview: Sprint C hotfix (2026-09-24, post-deploy user report): reverts the Path2D-batched Canvas2D spike submission introduced in Sprint "Integrity Lock" back to one beginPath()/stroke() pair per spike, keeping the geometry, color, and mirror-line math byte-for-byte identical to the pre-Sprint-A file (diffed and confirmed). The batched version composited each color bucket as one flat Path2D shape; separate per-spike stroke() calls at alpha<1 blend/layer wherever adjacent spikes overlap, which is what gave the ring its soft, glowing, "smooth fluid" look — losing that per-spike blending read as a real visual regression ("blocky"), reported directly by the user after live testing. The perf-win tradeoff was not worth an unrequested visual change to the app's signature look, so it is reverted; Chroma Flare (additive, lighter-composited) is kept as a pure addition on top, with its amplitude gate raised from 0.12 to 0.35 (flareAmpGate) — buf[] is spikeFeature.spikeDisplayBuf, the signal chain's own already-smoothed, already-gated (displayGate=0.07 in spikeSignalChain.ts) display value, so 0.12 was barely above the existing noise floor and let a sustained, non-transient reading in one narrow bin range (consistent with real microphone hardware noise floor, confirmed by the user as present even with Chaos at 0 and appearing in exactly one location that rotates as a unit with rotation sync, i.e. tied to specific bin indices rather than a coordinate bug) trigger the flare continuously even in near-silence. No spike geometry, frequency mapping, or the certified exact production frame body (executeVisualFramePipeline) is touched by either change.
recoveryReview: Recovery patch (2026-09-24, same day, after the user supplied their approved 'last known best' reference build and reported the spike ring as unacceptably degraded): three prior changes are fully reverted after diffing directly against that reference build, not against stored notes. (1) CanvasSpikeRingRenderer.ts is restored byte-for-byte to the reference — Chroma Flare (added in the sprintCHotfixReview entry above) is removed entirely; it was a wholly new visual element with no precedent in the reference, not a modification of the original band-recolor Iridize, and the user does not want it. Iridize is once again pure band-recolor with no added geometry. (2) createRendererViewportSetup.ts's shouldInitLegacyGL is restored to the reference's exact original expression (`!CORE_PARTICLES_SANDBOX && !useWebGLCoreParticlesRef.current`, i.e. always false, GPU spike path dormant) — two separate attempts to enable it (this sprint's hotfix, and a deeper resource-acquisition-safety investigation afterward) each looked sound in isolation but both broke in production the instant glCanvas actually rendered for the first time: a second, mispositioned copy of the spike ring appeared in the corner, because that canvas element's DOM layout had never been exercised with visible content before and its position was simply never correct. (3) AudioSystemInit.ts's analyser.smoothingTimeConstant is restored to 0.04, matching the reference; the 0.48 value applied in "Sprint Integrity Lock" came from a stored project note claiming it was empirically optimal, but that note predates this reference build and was stale, not the code. Outside this frozen set, the FFT-resize newLength in registerVisualizerControlPlane.ts is also reverted to timeArr.length (from analyser.frequencyBinCount) for the same reason: exact parity with the approved reference took priority over an unverified-in-production optimization. Net effect: every spike-ring and Iridize-adjacent change from "Sprint Integrity Lock" onward is now reverted; only the unrelated Sprint B changes (BPM worker, GIF export code-split, ParticleCubeField allocation fix, none of which touch spike rendering) remain. The exact production frame body (executeVisualFramePipeline) was never touched by any of this.
emergencyRevertReview: Emergency revert (2026-09-24, same day, minutes after the Iridize redesign patch shipped): that patch is fully reverted — CanvasSpikeRingRenderer.ts restored byte-for-byte to the recoveryReview state (diffed and confirmed, 29 lines removed, nothing else). Root cause: the redesign never called ctx.save()/ctx.restore() or reset ctx.strokeStyle around its new accent stroke, so Canvas2D persisted that accent color forward and it became the BASE line color for every subsequent spike until the next color-band boundary reset it. At low Iridize this made the leaked (near-transparent) accent color paint most of the ring nearly invisible; at high Iridize it washed the whole ring toward the bright accent hue. Reported directly by the user within minutes of testing.
iridizeSmoothGradientReview: Iridize smooth-gradient enhancement (2026-09-24, same day, third attempt, user-directed after seeing the reverted original band-recolor Iridize and confirming that direction — hard-edged color bands, not per-spike geometry — was correct, just needed two things: no visible seams between bands, and roughly 3x the intensity). Both changes stay entirely inside the existing band-recolor mechanism reverted to above; no new geometry, no compositing mode, no ctx.save()/restore() needed since strokeStyle is written fresh every spike now (see below), eliminating any possibility of the state-leak bug from the reverted attempt. (1) The expensive per-band math (trig, amplitude sampling) still runs only once per iridizeBandSize band, exactly as before — the three literal assertions live-session-stability.unit.test.mjs pins (canvasIridize, iridizeBandSize, the i % iridizeBandSize === 0 trigger) are unchanged and still present verbatim. What changed: each band computation now also stores its result as a target color (curBandHue/Sat/Lum) and keeps the previous band's target (prevBandHue/Sat/Lum), and EVERY spike (not just band-boundary spikes) does one cheap linear interpolation (circular for hue, to avoid the 350->10 degree wraparound taking the long way) between those two targets based on its fractional position through the band. This produces a continuous gradient across the whole ring with no hard seams, at the cost of one flat-color stroke per spike when Iridize is on -- the same per-spike strokeStyle-assignment cost pattern the spectrumMode branch two lines below already has, not a new one. (2) A new IRIDIZE_INTENSITY_MULT = 3 constant scales the color-shift intensity input (iriIntensity and the beatPulse hue/sat/lum terms) by 3x, per explicit user request ("even at 100% too weak, needs 3x, noticeable at 10-20%"); every downstream use was already clamped (Math.min(100,...), Math.min(76/85,...)), so scaling the input is safe and just reaches those clamp ceilings sooner, which is exactly the earlier-onset intensity that was asked for. The saturation clamp ceiling is unchanged at 100; the luminance clamp ceiling was raised from 76 to 85 to give the now-3x-stronger effect a bit more headroom at maximum before it flattens out. No RAF, timer, worker, or new per-spike trig was added; the exact production frame body (executeVisualFramePipeline) is untouched.
